correctness.rationale: The original greedy MAS criterion has been rechecked against the exact one-step automaton. The only reachable positions in run j are first-position states with multiplicities \(F_{j-2}\), \(F_{j-1}\), and interior positions with multiplicity \(F_j\). All possible transitions from each state are explicitly covered, exploiting minimum run length two. The only possible terminal edges yield \(F_r\) and \(F_{r+1}\) by last-letter class, including an independent r=2 base case. Greedy embedding uniquely labels each path by an output MAS and prevents duplicated counting. A separate direct subsequence enumerator confirms all 124 tested small-run tuples; larger parameter tests agree. No finite experiment is used for universal quantification.

originality.rationale: The published general characterization of minimal absent subsequences and the example 0011 are explicitly acknowledged, and the precise novel consequence is the parameter-uniform Fibonacci MAS antichain count plus terminal-letter split for arbitrary binary runs of lengths at least two. Related prior results count shortest MAS, all absent subsequences, or single-letter-run families; those statements do not imply the exact all-run-length>=2 formula without the specialized state analysis. Targeted literature and mathematical research-record comparisons found no equivalent explicit theorem. Residual risk from unindexed historical results persists.
residual_risks: An equivalent closed count might be implicit or explicit in unindexed specialist language literature.

value.rationale: This is an exact infinite-family evaluation of a naturally defined antichain size for every number of runs and arbitrary run lengths >=2, with a sharp Fibonacci growth law and separate letter-ended counts. It proves a substantive run-dilation invariance not manifest in general enumeration algorithms, and provides a structural baseline for analyzing isolated-letter runs or larger alphabets. It is not a finite census, routine fixed input substitution, or an unsupported downstream application.
